synopsis: NSGA-II (Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II), attributed to Deb and colleagues in 2002, handles multiple objectives by evolving a whole Pareto front; the glossary says evolutionary methods can produce this front in one run [f14420, f14413]. Chapter 9 recommends these methods for balancing misses, false alarms, unnecessary braking and stopping margin because they expose trade-offs rather than hiding them in one score [f7317, f6971]. The booklet describes them as robust and easy to parallelise over simulation, but requiring many evaluations [f6970, f14421, f6972]. Producing a Pareto front does not resolve the policy choice of an acceptable point, and trying many configurations increases over-fitting risk [f6973, f7320]. Recommended safeguards are nested validation, final-point selection using pre-declared safety constraints and independent-set confirmation; generic engineering evidence exists, but no specific off-road evidence is identified [f7321, f7322].
